transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, well... I guess what brings me in is that I’ve just been waking up with this really heavy, hollow sadness lately. I work as a choreographer, and the best way I can describe it is that it feels like... like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. It's just this very empty, sad feeling that I can't seem to shake.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this way in the past, or is this the first time you have felt like this?
Um, well, it's not exactly the first time I've ever felt down, but as for this specific stretch... this depressed part has been present for about nine months now.
During these past nine months, have there been any periods of a few weeks or more where you felt like your mood had completely returned to your normal, baseline self?
No, not really. It's just been this constant, heavy feeling the whole time. I haven't had any breaks where I felt like my normal self again.
Besides this persistent sadness, have you noticed other changes in your daily life, such as difficulty with your appetite, trouble sleeping, or feeling like you have very little energy?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely changed. Honestly, food just tastes like cardboard lately, so I haven't been eating much at all. My rehearsal clothes have been hanging a lot looser than usual. And, well, even before this sad period... when I was, um, buzzing with all those ideas and choreographing non-stop, I’d just skip meals without even noticing. So my eating has been off for a while.
During those times when you were buzzing with ideas and choreographing non-stop, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual to feel fully rested?

Yeah, my sleep has been all over the place. Um, back when I was really buzzing with ideas, I didn't need much sleep at all. Some nights I'd just stay up sketching formations until dawn and feel totally fine the next day. But lately, with this heavy feeling, it's different. I'll fall asleep completely exhausted, but then I just wake up at four or five in the morning with my stomach all tight, and I can't get back to sleep.
During those times when you were buzzing with ideas and needing very little sleep, how many days in a row would that usually last?
Um, it was a lot more than just a few days. That whole pattern of being up and buzzing... it actually started right after my ankle injury, and it went on for about two months straight.
During those two months when you were buzzing with ideas and needing very little sleep, did you find that you were talking much faster than usual or feeling unusually self-important or powerful?

Yeah, definitely the talking part. My collaborators actually told me I was talking so fast in our meetings that they couldn't even get a word in. I just... I remember feeling like if I paused for even a second, the whole idea would just completely disappear. So I just had to get it all out at once.

During those two months when you were buzzing with ideas and talking very fast, did you feel like you were capable of doing things that others might find impossible or that you had special talents or powers?

Yeah, I did feel like that. I mean, I honestly believed I could turn my ankle injury—this huge setback—into a career-defining piece. I thought it was going to completely change how people think about dance and the wilderness. It just felt so obvious to me, and I remember being genuinely shocked when other people didn't immediately see it the same way.

During that two-month period when you felt you had these special insights, did you feel that your behavior was so extreme or disruptive that you required hospitalization or were unable to function in your daily responsibilities?

No, I didn't need to be hospitalized or anything like that. But I definitely wasn't functioning like I normally do as a choreographer or a teacher. Things got pretty messy. 

I fell way behind on my teaching prep, and I actually missed a grant deadline because I was so focused on everything else. My studio just got incredibly chaotic, to the point where my collaborators had to step in and start handling basic scheduling for me. I mean, I was still showing up for the essentials, but I really wasn't managing my daily responsibilities the way I usually do.
During that two-month period, did you ever experience any hallucinations or hear voices that others couldn't hear?

Yes, I actually did. On a few of the days when I was the most wired, I could hear this low humming voice. It sounded kind of like wind blowing over a rock. It would tell me exactly where the dancers should move. And the thing is, I was completely alone in my apartment with all the windows closed when it happened.

This shifts the diagnosis from F31.12 (Bipolar I, current episode manic without psychotic features) or F31.81 to F31.2 (Bipolar I, current episode manic with psychotic features).
